doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening and the disputed birth year
summary: Interview opening, then Freeman explains why sources give 1922 or 1923 and how he set his own birth year for a passport.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: Funding for the Smithsonian Jazz Oral History Program NEA Jazz Master interview was provided by the National Endowment for the Arts.

Tuesday, May 23rd, 2000, 5:22 pm, Von Freeman oral history. My name: I’m Steve Coleman. I’ll keep this in the format that I have here. I’d like to start off with where you were born, when you were born.
Let’s see. It’s been a little problem with that age thing. Some say 1922. Some say 1923. Say 1923. Let’s make me a year younger. October the 3rd, 1923.
Why is there a problem with the age thing?

I don’t know. When I was unaware that they were writing, a lot of things said that I was born in ’22. I always thought I was born in ’23. So I asked my mother, and she said she couldn’t remember. Then at one time I had a birth certificate. It had ’22. So when I went to start traveling overseas, I put ’23 down. So it’s been wavering between ’22 and ’23. So I asked my brother Bruz. He says, “I was always two years older than you, two years your elder.” So that put me back to 1923. So I just let it stand there, for all the hysterians – historian that have written about me. Said it was 1922.
Yeah, at St. Luke Hospital. It was right down the street from where Fred Anderson has his place now, right down around, oh, I would say, 23rd [Street] and Indiana [Avenue].
Because, you know, you can order birth certificates here in Chicago, but if the birth certificate’s wrong.

Yeah, well, see, this one I made out. This was myself, because I was going overseas for the first time. So I had to have a passport. So I put down ’23. The man went and got something. He said, “It says ’22.” I said, “But it’s ’23.” He said okay. What difference does it make?
So the official birth certificate is something you made up.
